decisions.executionNote: Begin left-tube approach with an elbow-up lifting arc; adapt orientation to the visible diagonal tube.
Continue the left elbow-up arc toward the tube, turning the open jaws down and along its axis.
Lower toward the left tube with the jaws open; finish matching its horizontal axis before grasping.
Center the left tube using the wrist view, make a small axis correction, then close the gripper.
Lift the closed left gripper clear of the tabletop and check that the tube follows before rotating upright.
Tube follows the gripper. Begin rotating it upright while carrying it toward a left rack slot.
Finish uprighting the retained tube over the left side of the rack, maintaining clearance for visual slot alignment.
Align the upright tube over the leftmost large front slot and descend partway for a closer wrist-camera check.
Lower the centered tube slowly into the left rack slot, keeping the grasp closed until it is seated.
The tube appears to meet the slot rim. Lift slightly, make a millimeter-scale left/back alignment correction, and retry gently.
Release gradually over the aligned slot to let the tube settle, then retreat slightly to inspect its depth and uprightness.
Withdraw the open left hand to inspect whether the released tube has settled into the slot or needs reseating.
The first tube did not remain upright. Clear the view with the left hand before recovering and realigning it.
Approach the fallen tube from above with the open left gripper, retaining the elbow-up posture.
Move above the fallen tube and finish turning the gripper downward with safe clearance.
Turn the open gripper above the fallen tube so the cap will face upward after lifting; maintain clearance.
Continue the cap-direction correction while remaining above the tube.
Finish aligning the open jaws with the fallen tube's cap direction while descending to a pregrasp height.
Make a small wrist-view alignment adjustment before closing on the fallen tube.
Respect the wrist-wrap limit; keep orientation continuous, adjust the grasp center slightly, and close on the tube.
Lift the recovered tube and gently unwind the wrist away from its limit while checking retention.
The recovered tube is retained. Rotate it toward upright with a gradual wrist-unwinding motion, well above the rack.
Continue uprighting the retained tube smoothly while unwinding the wrist and preserving clearance.
Continue the same smooth rotation toward upright and bring the tube above the left rack area.
Complete the upright rotation and approach a revised left-slot alignment; inspect before descending.
Shift slightly left and back over the large slot, then lower to inspect the tube tip against the opening.
Descend carefully at the revised alignment, watching for tube movement relative to the jaws or contact with the rim.
Continue the slow insertion at the corrected position; keep holding until the tube is visibly seated.
The tube appears to touch the plate rather than descend freely. Lift clear, correct toward the front of the opening, and retry without releasing.
Refine alignment from the exposed ring: shift the tube a few millimeters toward the opening, then lower gently while retaining it.
Center the tube laterally on the visible large opening, then try a short, slow insertion while keeping hold.
The opening is now centered beneath the tube. Advance slowly to establish insertion depth before releasing.
The tube has reached the opening depth. Open gently and withdraw straight back to check whether it remains upright in the slot.
The first tube is visibly upright in the rack. Retract the open left arm while starting an elbow-up approach to the nearer right-side tube.
Return the left hand toward its origin and advance the right hand over the second tube with the jaws turning downward.
Finish the left return and position the open right jaws above the second tube, matching its near front-to-back axis.
Center the right-hand grasp nearer the tube cap using the wrist view, lower the final centimeters, then close.
Lift the second tube clear with the right hand, keeping the gripper closed and verifying that it follows.
Rotate the retained second tube toward upright and carry it toward an empty right-side slot.
Continue the smooth upright rotation with the right tube held, keeping the left arm clear.
Finish uprighting the second tube above the rightmost large opening and pause for alignment before insertion.
Lower the upright second tube toward the right opening, retaining it for a close alignment check.
Make a small left/forward correction over the right slot, then lower the tube slowly into the opening.
Advance the second tube a short distance at low speed while checking its position within the visible slot rim.
The tube is contacting the rim. Lift it clear and realign slightly left and back before retrying insertion.
The tip is now over the visible opening. Lower slowly at this alignment, retaining the tube until it is seated.
Use the visible front opening to refine the tube-tip alignment; lift slightly, shift right/forward, then retry a short descent.
Center the second tube on the exposed large ring with a small lateral adjustment, then descend gently.
The tip is centered within the right opening. Open the gripper gradually to let the tube settle, then withdraw to inspect.
Withdraw clear of the second tube and lift the open right hand to prepare for the final tube.
The second tube appears tilted after release. Return the open right hand above it for a controlled reseating attempt.
